idiom_name: node:net socket + length-prefixed framing stream + handler table
implementation_notes: Node provides the mechanism but not the roles: net.createConnection/net.createServer give a duplex byte stream, and the classic structure collapses into a small idiom - messages encoded as JSON or msgpack with a 4-byte length prefix, a Transform stream that reassembles frames, and a plain object mapping message type to peer handler, so the forwarder is socket.write(frame(payload)) and the receiver is the stream's data handler. That is the simpler local form of the same design; the explicit Forwarder/Receiver classes are still worth writing when the transport must be swappable or mocked in tests, or when several services share one connection. Reach for a library (Socket.IO, zeromq.js) when reconnection, fan-out or multicast are required, since node:net supplies none of them.
pitfalls: 'data' events carry arbitrary byte chunks - without explicit framing messages split and merge silently; a JSON.parse per chunk is exactly that bug.
A socket 'error' without a listener throws an uncaught exception and takes the process down; close and re-dial explicitly instead of relying on reconnect.
Dispatching on an attacker-controlled type field (handlers[msg.type]) is a routing injection risk, and Buffer.concat copies every frame - use an async iterator if that matters.
